task_instance: Task 2 (Financial Modeling) of the initiating-coverage skill: build the required Excel financial model for a sample company (fictitious 'Acme Robotics Inc.', since no live 10-K/market data is reachable offline) with all 6 mandated tabs (Revenue Model with product+geography breakdown, Income Statement with 3yr historical + 5yr projected P&L, Cash Flow Statement, Balance Sheet, Bull/Base/Bear Scenarios, and DCF Inputs feeding Task 3), using only locally-installed Python/openpyxl.
evidence: Wrote /tmp/.../exec_div/.../build_model.py using openpyxl (already installed: v3.1.5, verified via `python3 -c "import openpyxl"`) to construct a 6-tab workbook: Revenue Model (5 product lines + 4 geographies, cross-sheet formulas), Income Statement (20 line items, formula-linked to Revenue Model, computing gross profit, EBIT, EBITDA, net income, EPS for 3 historical + 5 projected years), Cash Flow Statement (CFO/CFI/CFF plus Unlevered FCF pulling from the Income Statement), Balance Sheet (assets/liabilities/equity), Scenarios (Bull/Base/Bear comparison table), and DCF Inputs (pulls projected Unlevered FCF/Revenue/EBITDA plus WACC and terminal growth assumptions, explicitly prepared for a follow-on Task 3 valuation). Ran `python3 build_model.py` -> produced Acme_Robotics_Financial_Model_2026-09-27.xlsx (16KB). Verified deliverable by (1) reloading the file with openpyxl and confirming all 6 sheet names and non-trivial dimensions (e.g. Income Statement A1:I23), and (2) independently re-implementing the revenue/COGS/EBIT/EBITDA formula chain in a standalone Python script and cross-checking computed FY2028E figures (Revenue $3,028.7M, EBIT $363.4M, EBITDA $469.4M / 15.5% margin) match the logic embedded in the workbook's formulas. Attempted a second, stronger verification path (headless LibreOffice recalculation via `soffice --headless --convert-to csv`) but soffice failed even on a trivial one-cell test file ('Error: source file could not be loaded', exit code 2) in this sandbox, so recalculation-based verification was not available; this did not block the deliverable since openpyxl's formula authoring and the independent cross-check were sufficient to confirm correctness. No network access, credentials, or external services were needed: financial statement structure/ratios and Excel authoring are all local-tool tasks. Task 1 (qualitative company research) and Tasks 3-5 were not attempted per the 'one representative task instance' instruction, and would similarly be achievable offline for Task 1 (markdown writing) and partially for Task 4/5 (matplotlib is installed for charts, but python-docx is NOT installed, `import docx` raised ModuleNotFoundError - a real docx file could still be hand-built via stdlib zipfile/xml if ever needed, so this alone would not necessarily block Task 5, but was not tested as part of this task instance).
